headline.text: Where treatment categories overlap, Etelä-Savo lags in crude recorded multidisciplinary meetings (0.2% vs 6.0% nationally), while crude curative treatment (23.4%) is not distinguishable from 27.0% nationally.

details.text: In overlapping treatment categories where a patient can have several treatments, Etelä-Savo's crude curative treatment share is 23.4% (95% CI 19.8–27.6; n=105/448) versus 27.0% (4009/14873) nationally, with the 95% confidence interval including the national value.

Because treatment categories overlap and a patient can receive several types, Etelä-Savo's crude shares are above national benchmarks for life-prolonging treatment at 36.4% (95% CI 32.1–40.9; n=163/448) versus 30.4% (4522/14873) and symptomatic treatment at 46.2% (95% CI 41.6–50.8; n=207/448) versus 39.5% (5871/14873), with 95% confidence intervals excluding the national values.

Etelä-Savo's crude share of patients with a recorded multidisciplinary team meeting is 0.2% (95% CI 0.0–1.2; n=1/448) compared with 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, with the 95% confidence interval excluding the national value, though this indicator measures HILMO recording practice from direct patient contacts rather than care.

Nationally, preliminary unpublished figures show lung cancer care takes 155 days on average from initial symptoms to treatment in Finland compared with 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark, comprising 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care.

headline.text: Etelä-Savo's crude no-treatment-record share of 23.2% is below 27.5% nationally, suggesting relatively complete treatment recording, but county shares are crude and public data miss key pathway stages.

details.text: Etelä-Savo's crude share with no treatment record within 12 months—which mixes untreated patients and unrecorded treatment—is 23.2% (95% CI 19.5–27.3; n=104/448), with the 95% confidence interval entirely below 27.5% (4089/14873) nationally; as an inference, not a finding, this is consistent with relatively complete treatment recording, making a low curative share less likely to be only a recording artefact.

Taulukko 11 gives crude county shares only, which have separate limitations: they are not age-adjusted—county-level age-adjusted shares appear only in Kuva 16, where national curative reference lines digitised from the figure at ±0.5 percentage points are 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women—and independently, they cannot be stage-adjusted because stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of patients.

A journal article found HILMO diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types, concerning diagnosis concordance only, while public report data do not measure symptoms or referrals, do not mention occupational health, and outpatient primary care visits are not included in the report's data.

Public data measure imaging only indirectly as diagnoses based on clinical examination alone in approximately 20% of patients, and while 93.6% of patients have a recorded specialist visit within 12 months, the report does not show when specialist visits or treatments start.

headline.text: The team recommends auditing recording completeness for multidisciplinary meetings, stage and drug treatment, tracking access times using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions, and standardising referrals and diagnostic-phase coordination.

details.text: The team recommends publishing county recording completeness for stage, drug treatment, and multidisciplinary team meetings and reading gaps as data-quality signals, since Etelä-Savo's crude recorded multidisciplinary team share is 0.2% (95% CI 0.0–1.2; n=1/448) versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, stage is missing for about 48% of patients, and national lung cancer data collection is currently incomplete.

The team recommends reporting access times from referral to treatment start using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 guidance definitions—which cover 16 cancers—with handover alerts, because the Health Care Act sets no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion and the Filha National Lung Cancer Programme's diagnostics recommendation with recommended time limits is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

The team recommends adopting a referral template and persistent-symptoms rule modelled on the KYS regional pathway document and naming a diagnostic-phase contact person—which regional pathway documents currently lack—as mentor insight notes weak referrals get lower urgency ratings and the STM roadmap's measure 1.2.3 plans care-coordinator guidance by 2026–2028 for county adoption by 2029–2031.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
rec:1.location: §1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact

rec:3.claim_text: Team recommendation 3: Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding. Publish, per county, how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded. Read county ‘gaps’ in these fields as data-quality signals first.
